---
title: Images for the ggtime paper
format: gfm
code-copy: true
---

Figures, icons and plots for the ggtime paper, an implementation of a grammar of graphics for temporal data in ggplot2 (see [ggtime](https://github.com/mitchelloharawild/ggtime) and [mixtime](https://github.com/mitchelloharawild/mixtime)).

## Repository layout

- `graphics/`: diagrams, icons (`graphics/iconography/`) and composed figures (e.g. the teaser and component icons), drawn in Figma or similar, or assembled from plots.
- `plots/`: programmatically generated plots (ggplot2 / ggtime), including SVG sub-figures in `plots/nyt-subfig/`.
- `external/`: figures reproduced from other sources, see below.
- `illustrations/` and `screenshots/`: hand-drawn illustrations and screenshots (currently empty).
- `src/`: the R code that generates the plots.
  - `src/paper-figures-code/`: one script per paper figure. Each starts with `source("src/paper-figures-code/setup-common.R")` and writes to `plots/` or `graphics/` with `ggsave()`.
  - `src/paper-ready-figures.qmd`: polished figures for the paper.
  - `src/chi26-figures.qmd`, `src/chi26-figures-CH.qmd`: earlier draft figures for the CHI26 submission.
  - `src/timeviz-pain.qmd`: examples of problematic time visualisation in ggplot2, and how ggtime handles them.

Run scripts from the repository root, as paths are relative to it. Packages are managed with renv (`renv::restore()`). The figures need current development versions of ggtime and mixtime.

## External sources

- `external/gus-lipkin-blogpost.*`: <https://guslipkin.me/professional-blog/2022-04-14-reordering-bar-and-column-charts-with-ggplot-in-r>
- `external/nyt-george-floyd.*`: New York Times graphic on George Floyd and homicide / police killings.
- `external/aigner-discrete-granularities.*`: discrete granularities figure from Aigner et al.
- `external/tradingview-candlestick.png`: TradingView candlestick chart.
- `external/PGoG/`: figures from the Practical Grammar of Graphics (PGoG).

## Submoduling Instructions

Run these commands from inside the target repo (i.e. the one you want these images to be available in)

To add the contents of the latest commit of the default branch of this repo as the folder `images/`:

```zsh
git submodule add git@github.com:mitchelloharawild/paper-ggtime-images.git images
```

Updating contents to match the latest commit:

```zsh
git submodule update --remote --merge
```

to match remote:

```zsh
git submodule update --remote --rebase
```

## Folder & File Naming conventions

Folders: see the repository layout above.

File prefixes:

- `plot-`: generated plots (`plots/`)
- `fig-`: composed paper figures (`graphics/`, and some in `plots/`)
- `graphic-`: diagrams
- `icon-`, `coord-`, `geom-`, `scale-`, `facet-`, etc.: grammar component icons in `graphics/iconography/`

## Useful ImageMagick Commands

Crop & transparent background:

```zsh
filename=filename.png
magick $filename -trim -transparent white $filename
```

For details see: <https://www.cynthiahqy.com/posts/imagemagick-basic-trim/>

## Setup pre-commit hook

To make sure this README renders every time you add a new commit,
move the file `pre-commit` to `.git/hooks/` and make the script executable:
`chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit`

To skip the render when you commit add the `--no-verify` flag:

```
git commit --no-verify
```

## Images

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| echo: false
#| cache: false
dirs <- fs::dir_ls(type = "directory", recurse = TRUE)

catImages <- function(folder){
  img_files <- fs::dir_ls(folder) |> sort()
  cat(glue::glue("{img_files}\n\n\n![{img_files}]({img_files})\n\n\n"))
}

for (folder in dirs){
    cat("## ", stringr::str_to_title(folder), "\n\n\n", sep = "")
    catImages(folder)
}
```
